put.description:
Idempotently create a scenario with a fixed id; no-op if it already exists.

Lets callers seed deterministic scenarios (e.g. the integration canary) with
stable ids across environments. Never overwrites an existing scenario, and is
org-scoped: a non-super-admin may only ensure scenarios in their own
organization, and an id that already exists under a different org is rejected —
so this cannot read or revive another tenant's scenario.

Returns:
    The pre-existing scenario, or the newly created one.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 when ensuring into another organization; 409 when the
        name is taken or the id belongs to a different organization.

ActionUrl.title: ActionUrl
ActionUrl.description:
Valid action URLs for suggestions that link to external pages.

VALID VALUES (external pages only):
- /knowledge-bases - Create/manage knowledge bases
- /integrations - Set up Salla, Zoho, etc.
- /webhooks - Configure post-call webhooks

NEVER use /scenarios - that's the current page!

CRITICAL - HTTP Tool is NOT an integration!
HTTP Tool is added directly in the Tools section of this page. Do NOT use action_url for it.
Only Salla and Zoho need `/integrations` because they require external OAuth setup.

BUTTON vs CLICKABLE ROW:
- Same-page sections (tools, prompt, etc.) → Clicking scrolls to that section. NO action_url.
- External pages → Provide action_label + action_url to show a button.

Examples:
    - "Connect to Your POS" → NO action_url (HTTP Tool is in Tools section, same page)
    - "Set Up Salla" → HAS action_url="/integrations" (Salla requires external OAuth setup)
    - "Sync to CRM" → HAS action_url="/webhooks" (Webhooks is a separate page)

CollectDigitsToolParameters.title: CollectDigitsToolParameters
CollectDigitsToolParameters.description:
Collects digits from the caller via DTMF keypad and/or spoken digit sequences.

WHEN TO USE: National ID / Iqama, phone numbers, OTP codes, account numbers—any numeric capture
where keypad input reduces recognition errors versus free-form transcription.

Two length modes, mutually exclusive:
- Fixed: `num_digits` set — capture exactly that many digits (IDs, fixed OTPs).
- Variable: `num_digits` unset — capture until the stop key, `max_digits`, or an
  inter-digit pause once at least `min_digits` arrived (amounts, order numbers).

DataExtractionEnabled.title: DataExtractionEnabled
DataExtractionEnabled.description:
Captures structured data from conversations for analytics and business intelligence.

WHEN TO USE:
- Client needs specific data points extracted from calls
- Business requires analytics on conversation outcomes
- Data needs to be stored in structured format for CRM/reporting systems

HOW TO CONFIGURE:
1. Define the JSON schema with clear property names
2. Specify data types: boolean, string, number, or enum (for multiple choice)
3. Add descriptive titles and descriptions for each field
4. Mark required fields - only fields critical for business value
5. Use enum for predefined options (e.g., contact methods, categories)

COMMON USE CASES:
- E-commerce: Discount acceptance, preferred contact method, product feedback
- Healthcare: Symptom severity, appointment preferences, satisfaction ratings
- Banking: Transaction types, complaint categories, resolution preferences
- Customer Service: Issue type, urgency level, satisfaction score
- Sales: Lead quality, interest level, budget range, decision timeframe

NOTE: Only include data extraction when the client needs structured data
capture. Not all scenarios require this feature.

IntegrationProvider.title: IntegrationProvider
IntegrationProvider.description:
Available integration providers.

`salla-tools` and `zoho-desk-create-ticket` require external OAuth setup and are
NEVER auto-generated in the output tool config, connected or not - suggest them
instead (see `Suggestion Categorization for Integration Tools` below).

**Suggestion Categorization for Integration Tools:**

   **Use `verification_needed`** (shows in "Action Required" section):
   - When user EXPLICITLY mentions needing Salla/Zoho in their business requirements
   - Example: User says "We use Salla for orders" but Salla not in active integrations
   - This is a REQUIREMENT the user stated - they need to set it up

   **Use `resource_linking`** (shows in "Opportunities" section):
   - When LLM SUGGESTS an integration that could enhance the scenario
   - User did NOT ask for this; LLM thinks it would be helpful
   - Example: For a restaurant scenario, LLM suggests Salla could help with order tracking

**Examples:**

User prompt: "We need Salla for order management"
Active integrations: None connected
→ DO NOT add a salla-tools entry to the tool config
→ ADD `verification_needed` suggestion: "Connect Salla Store" with action_url="/integrations"

User prompt: "Restaurant delivery agent" (no mention of Salla/Zoho)
Active integrations: zoho
→ DO NOT add a zoho-desk-create-ticket entry to the tool config
→ Can suggest salla as `resource_linking` (optional enhancement)

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description:

Members that restate a `DisconnectionReason` keep its exact name and value, so the
only genuinely new ones are `BUSY`/`DECLINED` (a split of `USER_REJECTED` that only
the SIP code can make) and `OUR_FAULT` (a collapse of the five infrastructure
reasons). Kept separate from `DisconnectionReason` because most of that enum is
meaningless as a retry rule — nobody writes `retry_on: [user_hangup]`.

ResourceLinkingSuggestion.title: ResourceLinkingSuggestion
ResourceLinkingSuggestion.description:
Opportunities: LLM-suggested enhancements the user did NOT ask for.

Shows in "Opportunities" section (green, dismissable).

USE WHEN external resource creation would enhance the scenario:
- Knowledge base: "Create a knowledge base with your product FAQs"
- Integration setup: "Set up Zoho Desk integration to enable ticket creation"
- NOTE: Attaching KBs is done from the scenario form, not the KB page.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION:
- User explicitly mentioned integration but it's NOT connected → use verification_needed
- LLM suggests integration as enhancement (user didn't ask) → use this type

EXTERNAL vs SAME-PAGE:
- For EXTERNAL pages: include action_label + action_url (shows button) (The only valid urls are: /knowledge-bases, /integrations, /webhooks)
- For SAME page sections: NO action_url (clicking row scrolls to section)

HTTP Tool is NOT an integration! It's added in Tools section (same page).
Only Salla and Zoho need `/integrations` because they require external OAuth setup.

Example JSON (external page - has button):
{"type": "resource_linking", "section": "knowledge_bases", "title": "Add Product FAQs",
 "message": "Create a knowledge base with pricing info.",
 "action_label": "Create Knowledge Base", "action_url": "/knowledge-bases"}

{"type": "resource_linking", "section": "tools", "title": "Set Up Salla Store",
 "message": "Connect your Salla store for real-time order status.",
 "action_label": "Set Up Salla", "action_url": "/integrations"}

Example JSON (same page - no button, clicking scrolls):
{"type": "resource_linking", "section": "tools", "title": "Connect to Your POS",
 "message": "Add an HTTP Tool in the Tools section to connect to your ordering API.",
 "tool_slug": "custom-api"}

trigger_conditions.title: Trigger Conditions
trigger_conditions.description: The single list of cases when a callback should be offered or recorded. The agent reads it during the call to decide whether to offer one, and the post-call analyst reads the same list to infer one when follow_up_inference is set. Callbacks, whether agreed during the call or created by the call report afterwards, can be at most max_wait ahead (the scenario's max_wait, never more than 29 days). A condition that implies a later date (for example a reminder the day before a payment due next quarter) is not supported and will be refused.
examples: When the customer asks to be called back later
When the customer says now is not a good time
When the person who can decide is unavailable

confirmation_messages.title: Confirmation Messages
confirmation_messages.description: Optional message confirming the agreed callback time, per language. Use {time} as the placeholder: it renders as the bare day and clock phrase ("3:30 PM", "tomorrow 3:30 PM"), so the template supplies the approximation word itself ("around {time}"). A bare {time} promises a minute-exact call the scheduler does not guarantee.

examples.en: Great, we'll call you back around {time}.
examples.ur: ٹھیک ہے، ہم آپ کو {time} کے قریب کال کریں گے۔

offer_callbacks_in_call.title: Offer Callbacks In Call
offer_callbacks_in_call.description: Whether the agent can agree a callback time during the call. When off, the tool is never registered with the agent (the agent never offers or promises live, and the scenario prompt handles the conversation normally); a customer's explicit request is still caught by the post-call analyst and booked.

requires_human_support.title: Requires Human Support
requires_human_support.description: Whether a human must be reachable during the callback. The AI still places the callback; enabling this constrains callback times to the transfer-to-human tool's working hours so an escalation mid-callback can succeed.

max_reschedule_attempts.title: Max Reschedule Attempts
max_reschedule_attempts.description: How many times a callback may be rescheduled across its lifetime (the customer answers a callback and asks to move it again). Changes of mind within one call do not count.

min_wait.title: Min Wait
min_wait.description: Shortest wait between now and a callback. Requests sooner than this are moved to now plus this wait, and the agent confirms the moved time. The same wait is re-applied after the call: a promise made early in a long call can fall under the platform's minimum booking lead by the time the callback is booked, and the booker moves it to now plus this wait rather than dropping it.

max_wait.title: Max Wait
max_wait.description: Longest wait between now and a callback. Requests beyond this are refused rather than clamped, and the agent asks for a nearer time. The ceiling sits below the platform's booking horizon, and booking time only moves closer to the promised time, so a promise at the ceiling stays inside the horizon.

default_callback_hour.title: Default Callback Hour
default_callback_hour.description: Local hour used when the analyst derives a callback time from a day-only anchor

follow_up_inference.description: When set, the post-call analyst may also infer follow-up callbacks from the transcript. Leave unset to record only what the agent agreed in the call.

ScheduleCallbackToolParameters.title: ScheduleCallbackToolParameters
ScheduleCallbackToolParameters.description:
Records a request to call the customer back later, during or after the call.

WHEN TO USE: Only when the prompt mentions calling the customer back at a later time
(customer asks for a callback, the right person is unavailable, a follow-up was
promised). Never add it by default.
BEST PRACTICES:
- Define 2-4 trigger conditions in English; they are evaluation signals, not spoken text
- Phrase confirmations as an approximate time ("around 3:30"): the exact dial time is
  decided later by the scheduler, so never promise a minute-exact call
- Use `{time}` in the confirmation messages as the placeholder for the agreed time.
  It is substituted with the bare day and clock phrase only ("3:30 PM", "tomorrow
  3:30 PM"), so the template itself must carry the approximation word: write
  "around {time}", never a bare "{time}"
- Set `requires_human_support` when the callback needs a human to be available too;
  it requires a transfer-to-human tool with working hours configured
- Configure `follow_up_inference` only when the business also wants callbacks the
  customer never asked for
- Set `default_callback_hour` to the local hour the analyst should book when the
  call fixes only a day ("call me tomorrow"), not a time of day

CALLING WINDOW: the callback calling window is the scenario's schedule configuration
(the `ScheduleConfig` row behind `schedule_config_id`, resolved through
`ScheduleConfigStore.resolve_scenario_default`). That is a single daily start/end
window with a timezone that may be null, in which case the scenario's own timezone
applies. The scenario may have no schedule configuration, a disabled one, or one with
no retry_window: all three mean no window, and only min/max wait apply. There is no
per-weekday map here, unlike the transfer tool's working hours (adding one is a
tracked follow-up). The tool carries no window and no timezone of its own.

NOTE: This tool only records the request; scheduling and dialing happen after the call.

ScheduleConfig.title: ScheduleConfig
ScheduleConfig.description:
One schedule_config row.

`retry_on=None` means the phase-1 default outcome set; `retry_on=frozenset()`
means "retry on nothing" and is a distinct, deliberate value — the two round-trip
separately. Never collapse them with a falsy check
(`config.retry_on or DEFAULT_OUTCOMES`): that turns "explicitly retry on nothing"
back into "use the default set".

ScheduledCallCursor.title: ScheduledCallCursor
ScheduledCallCursor.description: Keyset cursor: the (scheduled_at, id) of the last row of the previous page.

ScheduledCallListItem.title: ScheduledCallListItem
ScheduledCallListItem.description: One scheduled-view row. `created_at` is when the promise was booked, not dial time.

SchedulingAvailability.title: SchedulingAvailability
SchedulingAvailability.description: Whether the scenario editor should render its retry section at all.

StoredBatchCallDefaults.title: StoredBatchCallDefaults
StoredBatchCallDefaults.description:
Read-side shape of the persisted `settings_data` JSONB.

Deliberately lenient, for the same reason `DeprecatedBatchSettings`
(batch_call_store) is: a row written under an older contract must stay
readable. Reading through the write-time contract instead would make a
stale row raise inside psycopg's row factory, so `get()` 500s rather than
404s — and both callers only swallow 404, so the Create Batch page and the
admin page go down together for that org. The "Reset to platform defaults"
button that would clear the row lives on the page that just failed to
render, so the org cannot unlock itself.

Every write goes through `OrganizationBatchCallDefaults` below, so a row
only lands out of contract when the contract itself tightens.

is_primary.title: Is Primary
is_primary.description: Whether this is the primary success criterion. Exactly one should be True.

text.title: Text
text.description: Description of what constitutes success. Use bullet points with \n for multiple items in primary criteria.
examples: - Collected payment information\n- Confirmed payment date\n- Sent confirmation
Agent successfully created support ticket with all required fields

SuccessCriterion.title: SuccessCriterion
SuccessCriterion.description:
Defines a success criterion for evaluating call outcomes.

Success criteria determine whether a call achieved its business objectives.
They are used for analytics and quality monitoring.

- Could be tool-related: "Agent transferred to specialist when customer requested human advisor"
- Could be business-related: "Offered loyalty program benefits to retain customer"

STRUCTURE:
- PRIMARY (is_primary=True): Exactly ONE criterion that determines call success/failure.
  The text field can contain multiple points separated by newlines.
  Format: "- Point 1\n- Point 2\n- Point 3"
    - Single point: "Successfully collected customer feedback and confirmed satisfaction"
    - Multiple points: "- Collected customer payment information\\n- Confirmed scheduled payment date\\n- Sent payment confirmation"
    - With tool call: "- Collected issue details\\n- Created support ticket\\n- Confirmed ticket number"
  ALL points must be met for the call to be marked as successful.

- SECONDARY (is_primary=False): Zero or more additional criteria.
  Each secondary is a separate object. These are nice-to-have objectives
  that don't affect overall call success/failure status.

TOOL CALLS IN SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- As Primary: When tool call IS the main business objective
  Example: "Agent successfully created support ticket with all required fields"
- As Secondary: When tool usage is optional/supplementary
  Example: "Agent transferred to specialist when loan exceeded $100K"
- Not in Criteria: When it's standard operation (e.g., end-call is expected behavior)

CRITICAL DISTINCTION:
- Tool CONFIGURATION (messages, conditions) → Define in "tools" array
- Tool USAGE EVALUATION → Define here ONLY when it's a business objective

SuggestionSection.title: SuggestionSection
SuggestionSection.description:
Form sections that a suggestion can relate to.

IMPORTANT: Use the EXACT string values below - no variations!

- `first_message` - First message/greeting configuration
- `prompt` - Agent prompt/instructions
- `template_variables` - Input data given to the agent (NOT "template_variable")
- `data_extraction` - Data extraction settings
- `language` - Language configuration
- `knowledge_bases` - Knowledge base attachments (NOT "knowledge_base")
- `agent` - Agent Profile selection
- `success_criteria` - Success criteria configuration
- `tools` - Tools configurations (NOT "tool")

SuggestionType.title: SuggestionType
SuggestionType.description:
Types of suggestions to help users refine generated scenarios.

DO NOT SUGGEST (obvious or already visible):
- Tool configurations visible in form
- Standard defaults (back-channeling 0.6, timeout 15s)
- "Review the generated prompt/criteria" (user will see it)
- Language selection (user controls via UI checkboxes)
- Voice selection (user controls in Agent section)

SUGGESTION LIMITS:
- Maximum 3-5 suggestions total
- 1-2 verification_needed (critical placeholders only)
- 1-2 assumption_made (significant business decisions only)
- 0-2 resource_linking (genuinely valuable enhancements)

LANGUAGE RULES:
- NEVER use abbreviations: Write "Knowledge Base" not "KB", "Point of Sale" not "POS"
- Use clear, user-friendly language

MULTIPLE SUGGESTIONS:
You can have multiple suggestions per section. Example: 2 verification_needed for "tools" is fine.

TransferMode.title: TransferMode
TransferMode.description:
How a transfer-to-human hands the caller over.

COLD: dial the human into the caller's room and step out (current default).
WARM: agent-assisted — caller on hold, human dialed into a private room,
AI summarizes context, then the two are merged.

dtmf_triggers.title: Dtmf Triggers
dtmf_triggers.description: DTMF digits that trigger transfer (e.g., pressing 0)

transfer_cases.title: Transfer Cases
transfer_cases.description: List of cases when transfer should occur.
examples: When the customer requests to speak with a human
When the AI cannot resolve the issue
When there is a complaint that needs escalation

transfer_messages.title: Transfer Messages
transfer_messages.description: Optional message to play to the user before transferring. Supports multiple-languages

examples.ar: بحوّلك الحين لأحد المختصين. لحظة وحدة
examples.ur: آپ کو ابھی منتقل کر رہا ہوں۔ براہ کرم انتظار کریں۔

working_hours.title: Working Hours
working_hours.description: Working hours configuration. Transfer only occurs within this time range when enabled.

outside_working_hours_messages.title: Outside Working Hours Messages
outside_working_hours_messages.description: Optional message to play to the user when calls are attempted outside of working hours

transfer_trunk_id.title: Transfer Trunk Id
transfer_trunk_id.description: Specific SIP trunk ID for transfers. If unset, auto-selects from available outbound trunks.

caller_id_passthrough.title: Caller Id Passthrough
caller_id_passthrough.description: When enabled, the transfer call presents the customer's number as caller ID (inbound: the caller's number; outbound: the dialed number), subject to carrier acceptance. Falls back to the trunk default when the number is unavailable.

transfer_mode.description: How the transfer leg is established. 'cold' dials the human straight into the caller's room (default). 'warm' puts the caller on hold while the AI briefs the human, then merges the calls.

warm_summary_prompt.title: Warm Summary Prompt
warm_summary_prompt.description: Extra instructions appended to the warm-transfer briefing the AI gives the human agent before connecting. Only used when transfer_mode is 'warm'.

TransferToHumanToolParameters.title: TransferToHumanToolParameters
TransferToHumanToolParameters.description:
Transfers the call to a human agent when the AI cannot handle the situation.

WHEN TO USE: When users need human assistance for complex issues, complaints,
or situations the AI is not equipped to handle.
BEST PRACTICES:
- Define 3-5 specific transfer scenarios
- Include both customer-initiated (requests human) and agent-initiated (complex issue) cases
- Use reassuring transfer messages
- Configure DTMF trigger (usually "*") for instant human access
- Set appropriate working hours if the transfer destination has limited availability

TurnDetectionRecord.title: TurnDetectionRecord
TurnDetectionRecord.description:
Runtime turn-detection resolution persisted per call (PROD-458).

``type`` is the path that actually ran (``sarj_eou`` / ``livekit_v1_mini`` /
``vad`` / ``stt``); ``configured`` is the configured detector's discriminator;
``fallback_reason`` is set only when the configured path could not run.

UpdateScheduleConfigPolicy.title: UpdateScheduleConfigPolicy
UpdateScheduleConfigPolicy.description:
An update states the whole policy, so `enabled` carries no default.

`UpdateScheduleConfig.enabled` has none either, for the same reason. A default
of `True` here would let a body that simply omitted the field un-retire a policy
its owner had switched off.

section.description: The form section this suggestion relates to

title.title: Title
title.description: Short headline (3-6 words). REQUIRED, will be REJECTED without it!

message.title: Message
examples: Replace the placeholder with your actual support hotline.
You mentioned using Salla for orders. Connect your Salla store to enable order management.

field_name.title: Field Name
field_name.description: The form field identifier to update when user fixes inline

current_value.title: Current Value
current_value.description: The placeholder value that needs verification

fix_type.description: How the user should fix this: phone/text (inline edit) or time_range/boolean/link (scroll to field)

tool_slug.description: Tool identifier. Valid values: transfer-to-human, zoho-desk-create-ticket, end-call, code-switching, custom-api, salla-tools, ivr-navigation

action_label.title: Action Label
action_label.description: Button text for external page actions (requires action_url)

action_url.description: External page URL. Must pair with action_label.

VerificationNeededSuggestion.title: VerificationNeededSuggestion
VerificationNeededSuggestion.description:
Action Required: Placeholder values that need user verification.

Shows in "Action Required" section (orange, NOT dismissable).

CRITICAL - WHEN TO USE:
- ONLY for PLACEHOLDER values that YOU generated (e.g., +966500000000)
- NEVER for values the user explicitly provided in their prompt!
- If user said "Transfer number is +966555555555" → DO NOT suggest verification
- If user said "Working hours 10am-midnight" → DO NOT suggest verification
- If user mentioned a specific KB by name → DO NOT suggest verification

INTEGRATION SUGGESTIONS:
- User explicitly mentioned integration but it's NOT connected → use this type
- Include action_label + action_url to show "Set Up Integration" button

Example JSON:
{"type": "verification_needed", "section": "tools", "title": "Update Transfer Number",
 "message": "Replace the placeholder with your actual support hotline.",
 "field_name": "transfer_to", "current_value": "+966500000000", "fix_type": "phone",
 "tool_slug": "transfer-to-human"}

Integration example:
{"type": "verification_needed", "section": "tools", "title": "Connect Salla Store",
 "message": "You mentioned using Salla for orders. Connect your Salla store.",
 "field_name": "salla_integration", "current_value": "not_connected", "fix_type": "link",
 "action_label": "Set Up Salla", "action_url": "/integrations", "tool_slug": "salla-tools"}

VoicemailDetectionToolParameters.title: VoicemailDetectionToolParameters
VoicemailDetectionToolParameters.description:
Detects when the call has reached a voicemail or answering machine and responds appropriately.

WHEN TO USE: Include in outbound call scenarios where the agent may reach voicemail.
BEST PRACTICES:
- Set hangup_when_voicemail_detected to true to end the call immediately on detection
- Use message_before_hangup with a MultiLingualMessage for a fixed recorded message
- Use message_before_hangup with an LLMInstruction to let the agent generate the message

ZohoAuthorizeUrlResponse.title: ZohoAuthorizeUrlResponse
ZohoAuthorizeUrlResponse.description: Zoho consent-page URL for the browser to navigate to.

ZohoAvailableEventsResponse.title: ZohoAvailableEventsResponse
ZohoAvailableEventsResponse.description: Available Zoho CRM events grouped by module

ZohoCallableRecord.title: ZohoCallableRecord
ZohoCallableRecord.description: The subset of a CRM record (Leads, Contacts, ...) needed to place an outbound call.

ticket_creation_cases.title: Ticket Creation Cases
ticket_creation_cases.description: List of cases when a ticket should be created.
examples: When there is a technical complaint
When the customer requests a callback

ticket_formatting_instructions.title: Ticket Formatting Instructions
ticket_formatting_instructions.description: Instructions for formatting the ticket content
examples: Include customer name, issue description, and requested resolution

can_read_previous_tickets.title: Can Read Previous Tickets
can_read_previous_tickets.description: When enabled, exposes a companion tool that searches the customer's previous Zoho Desk tickets so the agent can identify existing clients and reference prior context.

ZohoDeskCreateTicketToolParameters.title: ZohoDeskCreateTicketToolParameters
ZohoDeskCreateTicketToolParameters.description:
Creates a support ticket in Zoho Desk for follow-up actions.

WHEN TO USE: When an issue needs to be tracked or followed up by the support team.
BEST PRACTICES:
- Define specific cases that warrant ticket creation
- Provide clear formatting instructions for ticket content
- Include instructions on what data to capture in the ticket

NOTE: Requires a functional Zoho Desk integration configured for the organization.

length.title: Length
length.description: Maximum number of characters Zoho accepts for this field. Used to constrain extraction so updates don't fail Zoho validation.

data_type.title: Data Type
data_type.description: Zoho's semantic field type (e.g. 'email', 'date', 'datetime'). Mapped to a JSON Schema format so extraction produces well-formed values.

system_mandatory.title: System Mandatory
system_mandatory.description: Whether Zoho requires this field to be present on create/update.

ZohoModuleOption.title: ZohoModuleOption
ZohoModuleOption.description: A module the org can point a webhook or a writeback sink at.

query_strings.title: Query Strings
query_strings.description: This custom field contains the query strings provided in the webhook URL.
